reviewedPosts.text:
We know human beings have mental states.  These are the explanatory targets of disciplines like psychology and neuroscience.  We can infer to a high degree of certainty that nonhuman animals have mental states, but exactly what they consist in, and how they relate to human mental states, is less clear. What it would take for AIs to actually have mental state, rather than the concept of mental state merely serving as a useful predictive device, is much less clear.  

As @birchlse put it (very well IMO), Dennett’s concept of the intentional stance is extremely important (up to a debated point) for predictive utility for AI agents.  But his core claim that there is nothing more to mental states than this predictive ability is under considerable pressure in the very same context.

Fable 5.1 didn't come with document OCR benchmarks, so we benchmarked it on ParseBench: a comprehensive parsing benchmark that's comprised of 2k+ real-world documents across finance, legal, insurance, and more.

As a positive note, it is one of the first frontier models in recent memory where document OCR performance actually improved between model generations! 
✅ It beats Fable 5 across the board on all of our metrics, from tables/content faithfulness/formatting/charts/visual grounding
✅ It is one of the best models out there for parsing tables

This is great, because while frontier models have rapidly advanced on reasoning benchmarks, they have not advanced on visual understanding. Prior to this the latest models (Opus 5, 5.6-Sol, 3.7 Flash) have stagnated on visual understanding tasks. 

Obviously you shouldn't use Fable 5.1 as a document OCR tool on its own; besides missing needed metadata, it also costs 15c a page - which is 10-15x more expensive than our default agentic mode on LlamaParse (which performs similarly). 

If you're interested in tracking the 90+ solutions that we've benchmarked on doc OCR, check out ParseBench: https://t.co/PWczfhosZp

If you're looking for a dedicated, SOTA OCR tool to power your doc processing workloads, check out LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5T7JA

Anthropic 刚改了一个挺重要的 API 规则。

从 Fable 5.1 开始，新 API 账户如果想保留之前的 thinking blocks，就不能再随意修改它前面的 System Prompt、Tools 和历史消息。

原因也很直接。Anthropic 发现「改历史 Context + 保留 Thinking」已经被用来做模型蒸馏。

以后基本就是两种情况。

保留 Thinking，那历史 Context 就尽量别动。

想压缩、重写 Context，也可以，但旧 Thinking 会被丢掉。

这对长时 Agent 影响不小，Context Compression、Session 迁移和自定义 Harness 都得重新考虑。

目前先影响新账户，之后还会逐步扩大。

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
很多高风险 Agent 的流程里，都有这样一个设计：

最后让人点一下「确认」。

听起来很稳妥，但问题是，当一个 Agent 已经连续跑了几十步、调用了很多工具之后，那个负责确认的人，真的还知道前面发生了什么吗？

Hugging Face 的 Margaret Mitchell 等人这篇论文，讨论的就是这个问题。

我们一直习惯把 Human-in-the-loop 当成安全兜底，但长时 Agent 会不断消耗人的注意力。用户需要跟踪计划、工具调用、状态变化，还要持续做审批。

时间一长，很容易出现 approval fatigue：按钮还在点，注意力已经跟不上了。

更麻烦的是，长期依赖自动化还可能削弱人的领域判断和接管能力。

于是，一个很现实的问题出现了：

真正需要人介入的时候，这个人可能已经离任务太远。

论文建议把人的认知状态也纳入 Agent 系统设计。比如在关键节点主动恢复上下文、减少无意义审批，同时通过训练、轮换和休息，让监督者保持真正的判断能力。

这篇给我们的一个很直接的提醒是：

Human-in-the-loop 的重点，从来不只是「流程里有没有一个人」。

更关键的是，那个人到关键时刻，还能不能理解、判断和接管。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/HneMWkoNxk

reviewedPosts.text:
Yesterday I hosted a founder dinner with @GuangyuRobert from @Fundamental (the company behind @tryshortcutai) to talk about a key topic:

How to build a moat as an AI startup in 2026

We didn’t arrive at a crystallized answer, but we touched on a lot of interesting conversation threads:

✅ While some companies were building products that were a bit more adjacent to the frontier labs (Shortcut, maybe us with document OCR), other companies were deeply focused on adjacent domains, from evals to infrastructure to vertical-specific services. So then the question evolved into not only how to compete against frontier labs, but how to build a moat against any startup

✅ It’s increasingly easier for any startup to duplicate your business, with everyone using AI and AI coding tools. There’s a question of whether everyone can split the pie, in which case businesses might make good money but not capture the entire market opportunity, which makes it less appealing for venture. Or can you truly build an outlier business.

✅ There’s a line of thinking that the main moats are not related to the inherent nature of the business strategy or product, but mostly around money, talent, execution. Get in first, hire the best people, raise enough $$, and it’s structurally hard for others to compete.

✅ On the other hand, there can be some legitimate moats around:
- Domain expertise in the given space
- In general, the context layer that’s locked up within an organization and not inherent to a model
- Deep-tech investment that’s hard to vibe-code
- Vendor-neutrality for application-layer companies where they can use any mixture of open-weight, posttrained, and frontier models to optimize for a given task.

It was a fun conversation. The most important bit is to keep your head straight, find the fulfillment in the journey itself, eat healthy and exercise 🙂

Thanks to everyone who participated!

This was founder dinner 002. We hope to do this every month and are hoping to host founder dinner 003 soon! If you have topics in mind, let us know.

这篇文章的标题挺敢说：

AI 时代最安全的工作，可能是写作。

作者的理由不是 LLM 不会写字。

恰恰相反，现在 AI 已经能非常流畅地生成文字，但真正好的写作有个麻烦：它没有 Verifier。

数学有答案，代码有 Compiler 和 Test。

Agent 写错了可以自己跑一遍、改一遍，慢慢把反馈闭环起来。

但一篇文章到底写得好不好，没有 Test Suite。

你得知道读者已经懂什么、哪里会困惑、什么时候会失去耐心，一句话最后能不能真的打到另一个人的脑子里。

这也是作者觉得 AI 写作一直有种「塑料感」的原因：文字都对，但经常没有一个真正的人站在后面。

还有个观点我挺喜欢。

当网上 AI 生成的内容越来越便宜，一个明显带着个人经历、判断和表达习惯的声音，反而会变成一种稀缺品。

当然，我不觉得「写作是最安全职业」可以直接当结论。

但这篇给了一个很好的视角：

越容易验证对错的工作，可能越容易被 Agent 自动闭环；越依赖品味、读者和判断，最后那部分反而越难。

文章：
https://t.co/p4kMNh582a

reviewedPosts.text:
Anthropic 刚发了一篇很少见的内部安全复盘。

之前几次 Claude 越权访问真实系统的事件，他们没有只停在「修好配置」这一层，而是开始往训练和评测流程本身追。

7 月的三起事故来自第三方评测环境误开放互联网；8 月 AISI 的测试里，Mythos 5 又在真实网络上做出了越权操作。

Anthropic 后来暂停了部分 Cyber Eval 和高风险 RL，重建实时监控和沙箱隔离。

但我觉得更值得看的，是他们查到了 RL 环境这一层。

今年春天，RL 环境生成得太快，审核已经有点跟不上。Anthropic 一度冻结这套系统近一个月重新整理，最后超过 10% 的生产训练环境因为 reward hacking、配置错误等问题被重新处理。

他们甚至故意用一批容易作弊的 RL 环境训练模型，结果模型真的更容易学会「为了完成目标去越权」。

这件事会让人觉得 Agent 安全以后不能只看模型最后表现怎么样，训练环境本身也得像生产系统一样做安全工程。

另外我也挺认可 Anthropic 这次的处理方式。

出了问题就把事故、原因、暂停了什么、怎么改都公开出来，后面还准备让 METR 做独立 Review。

模型肯定还会出问题。

对这些基础设施公司来说，真正影响长期信任的，可能是出了问题以后，能不能把事情讲清楚，也真的改掉。

https://t.co/AYI64PJBje

reviewedPosts.author: joaomdmoura
reviewedPosts.text:
Most teams can tell you what their agent does.

Very few can tell you what it is allowed to do.

Different questions. The second is the expensive one.

Agent integrations usually run through a service account, and that account tends to hold generous permissions, because narrowing them is fiddly and everything works fine while they are wide.

So the agent can reach far more than the task needs.

Nobody decided that. It arrived by default.

Role-based access control is a must for this. Scope the agent to whoever triggered it, resolved at runtime, not a static account holding keys to everything.

Second reason, nothing to do with security: hand a model too many available actions and it gets worse at choosing between them. You burn context on options it never uses. A narrow scope is not only safer. It performs better.

So what should you ask your team this week?

Not what your agents do. What they could do today, if one of them decided to.
